clue.text: Primate needed second in stream, jostling

indicators.note: in puts the word for a second inside the jumbled stream
letters of stream jostling one another end up in a new order

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A monkey needs a moment in a crowded, rushing brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' is the definition. 'Second' reads as a position, but it is the brief moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, which is a kind of primate.

clue.text: Article on the beast with halo, seen in the heavens

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article
a lion is a beast

explanation.surface: A grammar article meets a beast with a halo, a heavenly vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminous ring or spot in the sky opposite the sun is called an anthelion, a halo-type optical phenomenon.

clue.text: Doubtful strength?

definitions.meaning: a doubtful possibility is expressed by the modal '...', as in 'it ... rain'

explanation.surface: Is the strength in question really there?
explanation.definitionFit: The modal verb expresses possibility, so something doubtful is what one might do; as a noun it means power or force.

clue.text: Of lesser importance? Outbreak of BSE ruins vet!

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the letters that follow break out into a new order

explanation.surface: Mad cow disease spreads and wrecks a vet's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak of' scrambles BSE, RUINS and VET together. BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, the British 'mad cow' disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Subservient can mean subordinate, serving a lesser role than something more important.

clue.text: No rates revision? It's a crime!

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refusing to revise local taxes would be criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges the letters of NO RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betrayal of one's country, is a serious offence in law.

clue.text: Said to raise a smile

parts.note: photographers ask their subjects to say a certain dairy word so that their mouths form a grin

explanation.surface: A remark meant to make someone smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this word for a camera pulls the lips into a grin, the classic photographer's prompt.

clue.text: Senior officers naturally having longer leaves than most

definitions.text: naturally having longer leaves than most
definitions.meaning: a variety of lettuce grown with long upright leaves

explanation.surface: Commanders, by nature, get more time off than anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests time off for officers, but it is the foliage of the long-leaved romaine lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: COs are commanding officers; cos is also a lettuce variety whose leaves are long, unlike round lettuces.

clue.text: Once a beater, now an interpreter

parts.note: EX means former, once
a pounder is something that beats

explanation.surface: A former drummer has become a translator.
explanation.definitionFit: One who expounds explains or sets out meaning, so is an interpreter of a text or idea.

clue.text: Girl's laid up — purgative's needed

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means the word is set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: Anne's, a girl's name with its possessive

explanation.surface: A girl is bedridden and must take a laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' turns ANNES backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant extract taken as a laxative, so it is a purgative.

clue.text: Arms reversed for men only

indicators.note: reversed says the word for arms is read backwards

parts.note: gats are guns, slang for firearms

explanation.surface: Military weapons are turned around at an all-male event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns GATS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is one where only males attend.

clue.text: Priest bans fancy personal ornamentation

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or contrived, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman forbids parishioners from wearing elaborate jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the letters of PRIEST BANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Breastpins are brooches worn on the chest, items of jewellery adorning the person.

clue.text: A weed to annoy

explanation.surface: A stinging plant that gets under your skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging plant is a common weed, and the verb means to irritate someone.

clue.text: Wild bushman in socially acceptable portrayal of Neanderthal?

indicators.note: in sets the bushman's jumbled letters and the letter for socially acceptable together, one within the other
wild means unruly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in old British usage

explanation.surface: A primitive figure is depicted acceptably in polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges BUSHMAN, and U is set within the result: SUBH + U + MAN. U for 'upper class' is from a 1950s British debate on 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neanderthal is often drawn as a not-quite-human primitive, below modern people.

clue.text: Mensa snub is irritating for this entrepreneur

indicators.note: irritating suggests stirring things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tycoon is annoyed at being cold-shouldered by the high-IQ society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritating' rearranges MENSA SNUB IS. Mensa is a society for people with high IQs.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepreneur is someone who sets up enterprises, a type of trader in commerce.

clue.text: Doubts if unmarried lady is to embrace surrender

indicators.note: to embrace means the title for an unmarried lady wraps around the word for surrender

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
giving up, yielding, surrendering

explanation.surface: Uncertainty about whether a single woman will yield to an embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubts' is the definition; 'if' and 'is' are link words. 'Surrender' is the gerund, the act of giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: Misgivings are feelings of unease or suspicion, a synonym for doubts.

clue.text: Confused greylag's laying egg inside church drainage system

indicators.note: the egg goes inside the rearranged bird letters
confused means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the greylag (a wild goose) with its s kept as a letter
an egg is O-shaped, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A muddled goose lays an egg inside a church gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges GREYLAGS and 'inside' puts O within. Here the 's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargoyles are carved waterspouts that carry rainwater off church roofs, part of the run-off system.

clue.text: Spot medico at work

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medico
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Find a doctor busy at their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a small spot of liquid, like a drop of rain.

clue.text: Hospital workers suborn witness

definitions.meaning: attendants who do non-medical tasks on wards
to suborn a witness is to bribe or command them to give false evidence, to tell lies on demand

explanation.surface: Ward staff who bribe someone to commit perjury.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as ORDER LIES: to suborn a witness is to instruct them to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderlies are attendants in a hospital; read as 'order lies' they command false testimony.

clue.text: Growl coming from big narwhal

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deep rumble emerges from a large Arctic whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnar is an old word for to snarl, a dog's rumbling noise.

clue.text: Monarch and Frenchman break in on her

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
to intrude is to break in

explanation.surface: The Queen and a Frenchman barge in on a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ERMINTRUDE is the cow in The Magic Roundabout, a British children's TV show; 'her' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare pronoun stands for a female character, a famous cartoon cow.

clue.text: Maker of man?

parts.note: an old proverb says good behaviour makes a person what they are

explanation.surface: Who created humankind?
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Manners maketh man', the motto of Winchester College; the surface points to a creator.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite behaviour is said by the proverb to form a person's character.

clue.text: Wind force-10 to be created

annotationWithheld.why: Wind force-10 to be created (8): BE + GOT + TEN, but no reading makes 'Wind force' give GOT; likely OCR misread, scan not available

clue.text: Former high priest returned from banishment

parts.note: EX means former

indicators.note: returned means the priest's name comes back, read backwards

parts.note: Eli was the high priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: An ex-high priest comes back from being banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ELI backwards to ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's country, a synonym of banishment.

clue.text: Card game on Sunday? That's grave!

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the letter for Sunday

parts.note: ombre is an old Spanish card game

explanation.surface: Playing cards on the Sabbath is a serious business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts OMBRE after S. Ombre is a 17th-century card game for three players.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and serious, a synonym of grave.

clue.text: Stage horse

definitions.meaning: to stage a show or exhibition

explanation.surface: A theatre production featuring a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a play is to stage it, and a mount is a horse for riding.

clue.text: Race to power — economist is pursued by furious master

indicators.note: being pursued means the economist comes first and the next part follows

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a famous economist

indicators.note: furious means wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An economist runs for office chased by an angry boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges MASTER. A race is a channel of water, like a millrace, driving a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill stream is a channel whose flow drives a mill, a water race supplying power.

clue.text: Quite enough wine to turn the head

indicators.note: to turn means the word for the head is read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A good amount of wine is enough to make one dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask, a huge measure of wine.

clue.text: The French term it as one

parts.note: un is the French word for a or one

explanation.surface: The French call it singular.
explanation.walkthrough: UN is French for 'a' or 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one.

clue.text: The main issue -— temper

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: The ocean's offspring has a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To season wood or a person is to harden or moderate them, the verb temper.

clue.text: Clean up stains — that's tricky!

indicators.note: tricky suggests craft or difficulty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IE stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Getting rid of stubborn marks is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges STAINS with IE, the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise is to disinfect or make hygienic, a synonym of clean up.
